# Racing Setup Analyzer

> A case-centric vehicle-dynamics workspace that predicts handling balance, sizes spring / ARB / damper numbers, simulates a tyre stint, and — with real telemetry and a verified calibration — reports honestly-gated measured metrics. Every value is labelled by how it was derived; every blocked feature states why. Local-first, no cloud, no account, trilingual (English / 繁體中文 / 日本語) across the app shell and the analysis workspace.

It is an Electron desktop app (also runs in a browser) built on textbook vehicle dynamics (Milliken, Gillespie, OptimumG). The physics runs locally in plain JavaScript. It is aimed at FSAE, track-day and sim engineers who know the formulas and want to see how they turn into decisions — and to do so without overclaiming.

## What this is

- A transparent, model-grounded setup analyzer and lap/tyre-stint simulator.
- A case-centric workspace: build an Analysis Case (vehicle + setup + optional telemetry), run the model, optionally compare it against telemetry, and accumulate traceable evidence.
- Honest about provenance: outputs are badged Physics / Model / Measured / Derived / Heuristic / Unavailable, and every conclusion carries credibility, confidence, provenance, limitations, blockers and a next validation step.

## What this is NOT (never claimed)

- Not a professional race-engineer replacement; never presented as professionally validated.
- Not a full multi-body-dynamics (MBD) simulator — the model is a transparent linear/quasi-static balance model.
- Not a complete tyre model — coefficients are estimated unless you import your own Pacejka `.tir` (pure-slip lateral only).
- Not a GPS racing-line / lap-optimization tool — no racing line, no exact apex from position alone.
- Not a telemetry decoder for arbitrary binary formats — the production import path is CSV / canonical-JSON.
- Not a source of hardware "clicks" — no validated per-car click→rate mapping, so output stays in physical units (Nm/deg, N/mm, %).
- Not a MoTeC / commercial-analysis replacement.

## Credibility ladder

- Physics — closed-form physical relation (exact for the inputs). ≠ Model.
- Model — a prediction built from physics relations. ≠ Measured.
- Measured — derived from real telemetry; still confounded; machine-read provenance (synthetic / real / unverified). ≠ fully validated.
- Derived — a deterministic transform of inputs. ≠ direct measurement.
- Heuristic — a rule-of-thumb observation. ≠ a vehicle fact.
- Unavailable — not derivable from present evidence (shown blocked, with a reason).

Fail-closed always: when a required input or quality gate is missing, the capability is blocked with a reason, never approximated. Driver behaviour ≠ vehicle characteristic ≠ setup finding; correlation ≠ causation; prediction ≠ guaranteed result.

## Current capabilities (stable)

- Handling-balance prediction (understeer gradient, LLTD, roll gradient, ride frequency) — Physics / Model.
- Setup Advisor (rule-based targets) — Heuristic.
- Spring / ARB calculator — Physics / Derived.
- Tyre analysis + 21-tyre track-day database — Model / Derived.
- Lihpao G2 lap-time + tyre-stint simulation — Model.
- 501-car preset database (each parameter graded confirmed/documented/estimated/unknown).
- Telemetry observation from confirmed CSV channels (directional) — Heuristic.
- Measured understeer gradient K_us — requires confirmed telemetry AND a verified road-wheel steering calibration — Measured (kinematic, confounded).
- Model-vs-actual comparison; Setup A/B (predicted balance deltas, never a lap-time claim); quantitative recommendation in physical units; corner coaching (driver raw-steering behaviour only).
- Local-first Case Library (save / reopen / duplicate / archive / export-import); raw telemetry stays on device and never enters a portable export.

## Roadmap (planned, NOT current features)

- R3.0C — reference lap & corner-delta intelligence (cross-lap / cross-session comparison). In design; the in-app Comparisons panel is an explicit deferred placeholder.
- R3.0D — deterministic, evidence-backed virtual race-engineer decision engine.
- R3.0E — recommendation experiment & outcome loop.
- R3.0F — hardening, schema migration, release.

## Privacy

Local-first. Cases/sessions live in the browser/Electron IndexedDB on your machine. No cloud, no accounts, no analytics, no third-party telemetry, no tracking. Imported `.tir` / CSV files are read locally and never uploaded.
